subtopic: Cell structure and functions of cell components

lesson.title: Cell structure and function
lesson.body: All living things are made of cells, and every part of a cell has a job. The cell membrane surrounds the cell and controls what goes in and out. The cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid where many reactions happen. The nucleus controls the cell’s activities and holds the DNA. Mitochondria release energy from food during respiration. Ribosomes make proteins. Plant cells also have a cell wall made of cellulose that gives shape and support, chloroplasts that carry out photosynthesis, and a large vacuole that stores cell sap. Animal cells have no cell wall and no chloroplasts, and they usually have only small vacuoles.
lesson.audio_script: Every living thing is made of cells. In both plant and animal cells you find a cell membrane, which controls what enters and leaves; cytoplasm, where many reactions happen; a nucleus, which controls the cell and holds the DNA; mitochondria, which release energy from food; and ribosomes, which make proteins. Plant cells also have a cellulose cell wall for support, chloroplasts for photosynthesis, and a large vacuole filled with cell sap. Animal cells have no cell wall and no chloroplasts. Remember the exam trap: the cell membrane controls what enters the cell, not the cell wall.
lesson.big_idea: The cell is the basic unit of life. Each part of a cell has its own job, and the parts work together to keep the cell alive.

sections.heading: What is a cell?
sections.text: All living things are made of cells. Some living things, such as Amoeba and bacteria, are just one cell. A human body is made of trillions of cells working together. Most cells are too small to see without a microscope.

sections.heading: Parts found in both plant and animal cells
items: A thin, partially permeable layer around the cell. It controls what enters and leaves.
The jelly-like fluid inside the cell. Many of the cell’s chemical reactions take place here.
Controls the activities of the cell. It contains the chromosomes, which carry the DNA.
Release energy from food during respiration.
A network of channels that carries materials around the cell.
Packages and sends out substances such as enzymes.

sections.heading: Parts found only in plant cells
items: A rigid layer outside the membrane, made of cellulose. It gives the cell shape and support. It is fully permeable, so it does not control what enters.
Contain chlorophyll, the green pigment. Photosynthesis takes place here.
A large space filled with cell sap. It stores water and dissolved substances and helps keep the cell firm.

sections.heading: Parts mostly found in animal cells
items: Help in cell division. Present in animal cells and absent in higher plants.
Contain enzymes that break down worn-out parts and unwanted materials.
Animal cells have small, temporary vacuoles, or none.

compare.title: Plant cell and animal cell compared

lesson.example: Think of a compound house. The gate is the cell membrane, deciding who comes in and who goes out. The head of the family is the nucleus, giving instructions. The generator is the mitochondrion, supplying the power. (In a plant cell, the fence around the compound is like the cell wall.) This is an analogy to help you remember, not an exact copy of how a cell works.
key_terms: A small part of a cell with a special job.
Lets some substances pass through and blocks others.
The tough material that makes up the plant cell wall.
The green pigment that traps light for photosynthesis.
The watery liquid inside the vacuole.
lesson.exam_trap: The cell membrane, not the cell wall, controls what enters and leaves the cell. The cell wall only gives support and lets everything pass. Also, mitochondria release energy from food; they do not make energy. And plant cells have a cell membrane too, just inside the wall.
